title: Invoice card payment through browser, VPC and Stripe, with the webhook hop
persona: Priya, a backend engineer at a small invoicing SaaS, about to ask an agent to make the Stripe webhook path idempotent after customers got two 'invoice paid' emails, sketches how she thinks a card payment travels before the agent reads the code.
topic: how a card payment on an invoice ends up marked paid
realism: The classic layered request picture with trust boundaries drawn as boxes around boxes. The mistake she makes and fixes (Stripe answering the API synchronously) is the most common wrong mental model of Stripe, and the async hop (webhook, then a queue) is exactly where duplicate-processing bugs live.

steps.say: Okay, this is how I think a card payment on an invoice ends up as paid.
It starts on the hosted invoice page, the checkout page, in the customer's browser.
That posts to the Rails API, pay on the invoice.
The API calls the payments service, which I think is just a module inside the monolith, not its own deploy.
And that creates a PaymentIntent on Stripe.
Then Stripe says yes and the API marks the invoice paid.
Hmm, no, that's not right actually.
Creating the intent just hands back a client secret, the money hasn't moved yet, the real answer comes later on the webhook.
So Stripe calls us back on the webhook endpoint, and that's dashed because it's async, could be seconds later.
The handler doesn't do the work itself, it drops the event on a queue and returns 200 straight away, I'm fairly sure.
And a worker picks it up.
Moving the worker over so the database fits, and the worker is what actually writes paid on the invoice row.
The queue is SQS, payment-events, that's what it's called.
Queue to worker is async too, so that's dashed as well. Dashed means it happens later, not inside the request.
Browser on the left, everything in the middle is ours, inside the VPC, and Stripe is third party.
The webhook handler is the one thing in there Stripe can reach, through the load balancer I think.
This bit, the handler and the queue, is what I want to change.

steps.note: not sure if we verify the Stripe signature in the handler or in the worker
goal: worker idempotent on Stripe event id, we've sent two 'paid' emails for one invoice

story: the synchronous path is Checkout page -> API (Rails) -> PaymentService -> Stripe (create PaymentIntent)
she first drew Stripe answering the API directly ('result') and deleted it: creating the intent only returns a client secret, and 'paid' really arrives later through the webhook
dashed arrows mean async, happening later and outside the request: Stripe -> webhook handler and SQS -> worker
the frames are trust zones: 'browser' (the customer's), 'VPC' (ours: API, PaymentService, webhook handler, SQS, worker, Postgres) and 'third party' (Stripe)
the webhook handler enqueues the event on SQS payment-events and returns 200 straight away (she is fairly sure); the worker is what writes invoice.status = paid in Postgres
she thinks PaymentService is a module inside the Rails monolith, not a separate deploy, and named it 'payments svc' at first
the queue was 'event queue?' until she remembered its name, SQS payment-events
the circled part (webhook handler and queue) is what she wants changed: the worker should be idempotent on the Stripe event id, because one invoice got two 'paid' emails
she does not know whether the Stripe signature is verified in the handler or in the worker
the worker box was moved left only to make room for Postgres, not a change in meaning
partner_should_ask_about: where the Stripe signature is verified (handler or worker), which she typed she does not know
what happens when Stripe delivers the same event twice or SQS redelivers it: is anything deduplicated today?
how Stripe reaches the webhook handler inside the VPC (the load balancer she was unsure about)
whether anything besides the worker (e.g. the browser's confirmation) also marks the invoice paid or sends the email
